assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting reshaped trade theory, the measurement of gains from trade and the empirical agenda on firm-level data. The framework is now standard in teaching, in policy analysis and across adjacent fields such as macro and development. Few ideas in economics in the last 25 years have changed practice as broadly.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the central model. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exports versus FDI, and Helpman's earlier work built the monopolistic-competition foundations. Redding's contributions are important, but they are mostly quantitative and spatial extensions. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are important precursors, so the three-person limit forces a hard attribution choice.
assessment.maturity: The core papers are more than 20 years old and have been tested extensively. Trade has not been recognized since 2008, which leaves room for this topic.
uncertainties: Whether Redding, or Bernard, Eaton and Kortum, should be credited alongside or instead of the proposed pair.
Whether the committee would prefer a quantitative-trade framing (B037) or a broader trade prize including B047.
I have not independently verified the exact citation and priority record.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The structural estimation of differentiated-product demand and of dynamic industry models transformed empirical industrial organization. It is also now used in merger review, antitrust, trade, health and environmental economics. Its methodological reach beyond IO is large and well documented.
assessment.attribution: The BLP demand framework (Berry; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes) is the clearest core. Pakes also has foundational dynamic-model work (Ericson-Pakes, with Benkard and others). Bresnahan and Reiss made important entry and competition contributions, and the long list of credited names means some deserving contributors would be left out.
assessment.maturity: The methods date from the 1990s and have had decades of application and refinement, and the practical impact is well established.
uncertainties: Whether Bresnahan should displace one of the three, given his independent contributions.
The committee may judge the contribution as methodological rather than as a discovery about the economy.
I work in a neighbouring field, so my views on its relative importance may be biased. I do not adjudicate that here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work reframed the debate on technology, trade and labour demand through task-based thinking, job polarization and the local labour-market effects of import competition. It has had very large academic and policy influence on how trade and automation shocks are understood.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the China-shock work, and Hanson to the trade-shock side. Katz has long-standing work on skill demand and wage structure. Dorn is a key coauthor of the China-shock papers, and Acemoglu's recent prize on related topics complicates the credit.
assessment.maturity: The foundational papers date from 2003 to 2013, and the China shock findings have been widely replicated and debated. Subsequent work has qualified some of the magnitudes.
uncertainties: Overlap with Acemoglu's technology work, and with Goldin and Katz's skill-demand work (Goldin was recognized in 2023).
Whether the empirical findings are seen as a discovery or as a high-impact application.
Dorn versus Katz for the third slot.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work made adverse selection and moral hazard empirically measurable in insurance markets. It moved from theory to credible estimates of welfare costs, with strong policy relevance for health insurance design. It links contract theory, which has already been recognized, to data.
assessment.attribution: Einav and Finkelstein have been the main joint drivers of the measurement agenda, including the cost-curve framework for selection. Salanie contributed testing methods for asymmetric information in insurance, and Chiappori and Salanie's positive-correlation test is a precursor.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from roughly 2005 to 2020. The impact is substantial but still being consolidated, and the field is less mature than the trade or IO methods.
uncertainties: Maturity and whether the recognition is premature relative to earlier-cohort candidates.
Whether Salanie or Chiappori should be credited for the testing precursor.
Firm-specific policy generalizability beyond health insurance.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal approach to the open economy built the micro-founded workhorse for international macroeconomics, in the Redux model and the standard graduate textbook. The 'exchange-rate disconnect' papers framed the central puzzles of the field. They shaped how researchers and policymakers analyse current accounts, exchange rates and policy spillovers.
assessment.attribution: The Obstfeld-Rogoff partnership is the clearest attribution on this list, with a joint textbook and the key models. Rogoff is also in B031, so the credit overlaps with his financial-crisis history. Others such as Svensson, Sachs and Dornbusch contributed to related frameworks, and Dornbusch has died.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1990s and is well established. Many puzzles remain unresolved, which weakens the claim to definitive discovery.
uncertainties: Whether unresolved puzzles reduce the strength of the claim.
Overlap with Rogoff's other contributions might dilute the attribution.
Recent macro prizes may weigh against another macro award.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work showed with granular data that household leverage and credit supply expansions drive booms, busts and the depth of recessions. It reoriented the post-2008 literature and added an empirical micro-to-macro bridge to the financial-crisis work recognized in 2022.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the joint core of the work. Campbell is a major household-finance scholar, but his contribution is on a different topic, so I do not propose him for this discovery.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from about 2009 to 2018. The work is influential, but it is younger than the earlier candidates and some causal interpretations remain debated.
uncertainties: Relative recency, and ongoing debate about the credit-supply interpretation.
Possible overlap with the 2022 prize for banking and financial crises.
Campbell's listing suggests a broader framing that I have not endorsed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities provides the standard structure for monetary policy analysis in central banks. It includes the Taylor rule, the micro-founded policy analysis of Woodford and Gali, and the Calvo pricing mechanism. The practical impact on policy is exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Attribution is the main difficulty, since the framework is cumulative and has more than eight credited names, including Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum, Evans, Gertler, Smets and others. Taylor (1993 rule, staggered contracts), Woodford (the integrated framework) and Gali (the empirical and theoretical development) are a defensible three, but any selection leaves out major contributors.
assessment.maturity: The work dates from the 1980s to the 2000s and is very well established, although the 2008 crisis and the 2021-22 inflation episode tested parts of the framework.
uncertainties: A very diffuse attribution and the three-laureate cap.
The framework's mixed performance in recent inflation episodes.
My expertise is in micro-founded pricing, which makes price-adjustment issues salient to me, so I discount my own view of this framework.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-run series on top incomes and wealth, built from tax data, changed the evidence base and public debate on inequality. This is a data-and-measurement achievement with large influence on public economics and policy discussion.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez established the top-income series, and Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson, a central earlier figure in the field, has died. Saez also appears in B035, so the credit overlaps.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from the early 2000s and has been extended since, but the wealth and offshore estimates are still debated.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over the wealth and capital-income estimates.
Whether the committee treats data construction and a policy-influential synthesis as sufficient scientific discovery.
The extent to which advocacy or policy roles affect the committee's view.
